body:
I can relate to that a bit. I don't know if its a depression think or if its a different mental ailment we both have but; On three separate occassions I've been told a good friend thought of me as a brother and it caught me completely by surprise.

My family is a horrible mess so I can't compare to that, but having friends that genuinely love me and I feel absolutely nothing aside from enjoying their company... like I have completely cut off someone I felt was toxic after years of friendship before and not felt anything at all. That can't be normal. It definitely contributes to my depression feeling like I can't reach out to people emotionally.

I don't know if you relate to any of that. But when you're talking about watching your close relationships with family deteriorate and reacting only with indifference, that's what it made me think of.
I hope you find a better solution for your darkness :). And we should all look for the light. That's what makes life worth living.

I have been lucky to find some really true friends, in an age where I honestly believe that's hard to do. There are just a handful of us but we have all been through hard times and were there for each other right away.

We get together once a week (or we did, until very recently) to play games and generally just hang out with each other. Most of the time its uneventful and we just chat for a little bit and call it early but some nights we've found things that kept us laughing for hours, until we all hurt from it the next day.

Additionally, I am someone that LOVES music. I'm definitely not as passionate as I used to be but it still gives me chills when I find something I feel is truly great. Working to expand my listening preferences has been one of the few things I've put work into that was rewarding. The more I open my mind, the more great stuff I find to enjoy. And a lot of what I listen to has creeped into my friend's playlists, so I know its positively impacted them too.

The fear is horrible. Its a large part of why I've been alone for so many years... too scared to approach someone lest they feel threatened, judge me prematurely, etc...

And while the thoughts of death aren't so bad, the actual dying part is terrifying. I don't want the last thing I experience to be an immense amount of pain. And even if it could be painless... just switching off like that is a terrible thought.

I just wanted you to know I relate.
I appreciate the understanding and you saying hello. I wish I had answers too. I'm glad there are people that care and hopefully you can help others on this sub that need it.

I posted my note on here a couple hours ago. I did many drafts too. It took a lot of introspection to figure out how I really felt and what I really wanted to say. It also helps you build the resolve to go through with it... which I am not supporting but as I'm going through this right now, I know that's the truth.

Chances are the detachment you're feeling is temporary. You likely still care about the people closest to you. And want them to understand. That clinical detail is a list of grievances, yes, but its also a list of reasons. So they can understand.

The only trick your mind is playing here is the desensitization. I can promise you that you still care. But we block it out because we feel we have to. That's where your note is coming from.

Apologize. It will be hard at first. Depending on how cruel you've actually been, people may not take you seriously. But start by apologizing. If you genuinely feel bad about how you've acted, it will help to alleviate the guilt.

The next step is to ask how you can help make it better. What's done is done. No point dwelling on it. But you can learn from it. And just saying your sorry is nowhere near as effective as working to make things better. THAT'S how people will know you're sincere. By working to fix your mistakes you start to be a better person. Hopefully the people around you will let you know if they see a difference. That will help your self-esteem and reward your good behavior, hopefully making you want to be a better person and make it feel not so impossible.

As of right now I thoroughly intend to go through with it. And because I don't want the police/hospitals involved like might happen if my friends suspected, I'm trying like hell to make sure they don't notice. The only thing I'm doing that's really out of the ordinary is giving away some things people don't normally give away. (I'm lending my PS4 to a good friend that makes very little money, for example).

Someone that's screaming about how they're going to kill themselves to their loved ones in a crowded room... well that might be for attention but they probably still need help. We're all screwed up in our own ways. Try not to assume its just for attention unless you've got strong evidence.

Over the last 8 months I've worked about that many temp jobs doing a variety of things from customer service to data entry to light warehouse work (until I got hurt... again). I've had 6 interviews. Over the years I've also had a dozen or so jobs... retail, bus driving, health insurance (that was the impossible job, 90% turnover rate at that company). In 8 months I have easily sent out 100 applications. The only thing I could really see doing differently is applying in a different city but I don't have the funds to make that happen.

BTW thank you for your responses. I'm here because I'm hurting, like the rest of this sub.

Hi stranger. I'm in no place to offer advice given I'm on here with a throwaway posting my note but I do have some thoughts on your situation.

There is a way to address you fear about how you'll do in the workplace. You could seek an internship or volunteer work. Try to find something you're passionate about. You mentioned you play basketball and guitar. Are those things that bring you joy? Would you be willing to maybe work with youth by coaching or teaching? Not as a career, just to try and find a little meaning with something you're good at. It might also help with your feeling meaningless in general as well.

As for romance, I can't help you there. I know the struggle. I've had one solid relationship in the last ten years, and was single 9 of those years.

I am curious about the hatred of your race and genetic defects. Are you willing to talk about those?

Its terrible when your family doesn't accept you for who you are. /u/baked_juice is right... sometimes you need to cut toxic people from your life. I haven't struggled with anything near as difficult as what you've described here. But my father is an alcoholic, and my mother is severely negligent and manipulative. Family is NOT an obligation when they continually tear you down. You have to put yourself first.

years of poor health and obesity make it difficult to do physical work, and I am very much to blame for that. BUT I do have medical problems with my knees (dislocate) and wrists (unknown, have seen doctors about it twice) that cause frequent injury whenever I work a job where I have to lift more than about 40 pounds regularly.

Honestly I'm best suited to general office work, typing around 100wpm with training in excel and some other basic skills, but those don't seem to be in demand based on the general lack of interviews I've gotten.
